title: Add per-chunk budgets on top of the aggregate eager-closure ceiling — vendor-objectstack (38%) first — ruled follow-up of #5468
body:
Work card created by the triage seat executing the maintainer's #5468 ruling. Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat 2026-08-21, verbatim 「其他接受」 accepting the triage recommendation for #5468 — **A now + C next, B rejected**: the absolute aggregate ceiling stays as shipped (PR #5466); this card delivers C, per-chunk budgets, so a single chunk cannot grow unnoticed inside aggregate headroom.

## Scope (S-size per the #5468 clause)

- Extend `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` (or a sibling in the same gauge) with per-chunk gzipped ceilings for the largest eager chunks — at minimum `vendor-objectstack` (1,493 KB / 38% of closure), `framework` (484 KB), `ui-components` (380 KB) — set truthful-current-state + small headroom, same discipline as the aggregate ceiling (no unilateral lowering).
- Chunk names/sizes come from the shipped gauge's own measurement (`eager-closure` report), not hardcoded expectations that rot — pin the mapping loudly if a chunk disappears/renames.

## Constraints from the ruling

- ⛔ No main-comparison ratchet (option B) — rejected for its merge-queue double-ejection failure mode and per-PR build cost.
- Baseline values need one fresh measurement at implementation time; if the #5325 / #5359 cleave work lands first, set the per-chunk lines after it, not before (the #5468 facet block's recorded caveat).

Refs: objectui#5468 (decision card, closing) · #5324 / PR #5463…#5466 (the gauge) · #5325, #5359 (cleave direction).
